reviews.text: [H1]ROGUE FLIGHT 是我的2024年度Steam Deck游戏冠军 [/H1] 玩了2小时，打穿了一条beta线，真该推荐。 就是说，制作组里有人能想出 [i]高出力引擎甩尾，用尾流作为AOE手段[/i] 这种天才的点子，它这个游戏就肯定行啊。 [SPOILER] 这一招，就像我当年看Z高达 卡缪用光束军刀放粒子电风扇清浮游炮 一样惊为天人 [/SPOILER] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3354890154 我打开Truant Pixel, LLC的主页，两个VR小游戏，一个乙女向游戏，一点也没有铺垫，却弄出一个极为扎实的街机飞行射击游戏。 出色的画面张力匹配战斗时的速度感，整体80~90s日漫的致敬风格[SPOILER]（虽然一眼欧美仿制，但这种模仿感也独有魅力）[/SPOILER] 关键词是 Macross 和 飞跃巅峰。 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3354947510 刚刚洗澡的时候回味了一下感觉剧情还是有可以说的东西： [spoiler] New game模式下，游戏总是从教学模拟开始，我倾向于女主角在NG模式下从未真的离开过模拟，α β γ线都是一种针对行为的未来预测，而每次结束之后，娜缇雅都会在驾驶舱内惊醒。 而NG+模式，arrow战机完全装备模式时，才是真正的决战。（另外arrow战机全装备型，感觉像是万代卖胶时候做出来的行为 笑） [strike]另外不会又要给我搞敌我同源吧。[/strike] [/spoiler] Steam Deck全程60帧，已然机主必买游戏。 中期机体性能不足后，靠积攒点数解锁改装获取更高的数值，严格来说比较rougelite。 本想强行找个不满意的点说它没有日配，但其实它有，而且请来了我很喜欢的三石琴乃， 顶级。 [H1]综上所述，没有任何不满意的，完美游戏真的存在。[/H1] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3354947656

配音质量很高（我选的日语），画面表现出色，场景和大型物件很震撼。难度可以调，一开始玩简单难度比较好，毕竟小机枪有点太弱了。可以自动回血，容错率较高。 甩尾攻击让人眼前一亮，是很好用的aoe而且cd很短，如果慢动作不嫌烦可以经常用。导弹反而没什么用，载弹量小且伤害低。 4个结局，主线3个，new game+有1个，不过多周目的过程重复度很高，new game+会出现新的关卡（其实区别也没有太大），另外全武器解锁必须先多周目，在new game+才能携带全部武器。 全结局通关后有16bit BGM可选，但我觉得要是一开始能选就更好了。

A highly stylish shooter that has some killer aesthetics and great voice acting, but unfortunately is tied to an incredibly bland and ultimately boring gameplay experience. Each stage takes thrice as long as it needs to, with fairly boring enemy patterns and capped off with a boss fight that has a tendency to use one attack pattern until you destroy bits and bobs, then shift into one more. None of the patterns are visually impressive nor are they interesting to deal with and the gameplay lacking excitement absolutely kills the mood the game is attempting to go for. It's really unfortunate because it has everything a shmup needs to be a killer game except for the actual game part. And the gameplay mechanics it attempts to add to spice things up ends up being little more than fluff. In many scenarios I'd be willing to look past the gameplay portion being lacking if it was trying to do something unique or different but what's here is a sub-standard shmup with poor stage design and even poorer boss design. I still hope you find success, but I cannot recommend it currently.

Star Fox 65 - Furry-Free Edition But seriously, Rogue Flight is a compact homage to games like Star Fox 64 and Space Harrier. While it pushes the envelope mechanically in some key ways, it isn't quite as expansive as Star Fox (no subs or tanks in this game). It's worth playing if you're fan of Star Fox, though it would be nice if there was an option to skip the first 2 missions before the level split because seeing the true ending, assuming you clear each route on your first try, will have you play those missions 3 times each - which is 6 repeated missions. Overall, the game is recommended with a grade of: B

I wish Steam had something between recommending a game and not. This is not a *bad* game, but it is not one I would recommend to others or believe is worth its release price of $20. Flashy presentation but very shallow gameplay and uninteresting enemies. You'll experience all of the game's mechanics in the first 10 minutes, and the story doesn't do much to keep things interesting. You're forced to complete the game four times to see all of it, with the final two runs barely adding anything of note. Buy it on sale and enjoy a little bit of nostalgia, but don't expect to get more than an hour or two out of it.

Found this game thanks to youtube music when the radio played a song by Rinn. Man am I glad I gave it a shot! This game is simple and fun! The game has that nostalgic factor while being modern and I love what the devs did with the story. It's short, to the point and man that ending though! Especially with the soundtrack which really helps so much with the style the devs are going for. It's also really easy to pick up for a level but also fun enough to keep playing for a good session, even more so since I don't have much spare time! I really appreciate the fact that I'm not expected to spend hours to play like most modern games. Not only has Rogue flight a permanent spot on my C:/ drive, but also a spot in my heart for those rainy days. PS. I hope the devs release purchasable OST. I freaking love the OST player in the game but man do I wish I could listen to the soundtrack while out and about!

这个很好玩啊！ 像素风格的街机飞行射击游戏，非常有日系机器人动画的感觉。剧情基本上来说就是宇宙骑士，只不过把拉达姆换成了天网。由于没有了拉达姆自然也就没有Tekkaman和D-Boy，所以你只能自己开着蓝色地球号把敌人都干死……顺带一提你也不是诺亚尔，你是葛城美里。我没打完全部路线，可能后面还有什么隐藏剧情，但大体就是这样。游戏里有分支路线，分别是去打A、去打B和……去把AB都打了。我先选的去把AB都打了再重打另一条线，结果好像内容没太大区别。可能Newgame+模式会有？ 玩法上是很传统的开飞机biubiubiu游戏。抠住扳机可以无限开火、捡到新武器可以子弹变发波发激光、有导弹、有滚筒闪避，比较有新意的加入了一个漂移攻击——战斗机一个慢动作大甩尾回避之后用机翼划出的轨迹打爆敌人（朋友说是尾焰，但我感觉好想也不太像）。听起来很不科学是吧，我也这么觉得，但强袭自由都能放轰天雷，我战斗机放个剑气怎么了？游戏的难度适中，手残如我通关也没问题。不足的是有些BOSS战的里BOSS的可以被攻击部位不是很显眼，我得先射一发导弹看它锁定在哪儿才知道应该打什么位置。 游戏的流程不算长，但制作非常精美，我认为值得一玩。

To be honest, I was conflicted about recommending this or not. I felt a bit cheated when I bought the game. I expected a StarFox-like game with roguelike mechanics (you know, from the name), routes to choose, meaningful decisions to make, randomized equipment, and proper progression after dying. What I got was just a side-scrolling (but in 3D) fighter shoot-'em-up with no real depth. After playing it, I can't even call it a StarFox clone. Gameplay is fast and fun—for a bit—until you realize the game isn’t difficult at all. The fast-moving background you see in the videos is cool and all, but it’s just that—a background. It doesn’t interact with the player in any way. It’s so poorly implemented that you’ll see giant asteroids coming at you that never hit, and ships that could cover the entire screen appearing tiny in front of the massive moving background the game uses. Sometimes, because of this, my brain ends up hurting. I’ve only experienced something similar in VR games with bad perspective handling. Any other game would clip things into perspective. That said, this game feels like a pretty decent demo title for your Steam Deck. It runs flawlessly. VHS filter looks great in a small screen. But still, you won’t play this game for more than 5 hours. You can finish it in less than a day. Maybe with a 50% discount, it would be worth it.

It's a very watered down version of a Star Fox game. Looks are alright, voice acting is good, but the level design is barely there. In fact, the game design is not particularly good. For instance, you unlock modules to improve your ship: speed/manoeuvrability, and weapons systems. The best modules give you greatly increased manoeuvrability, which translates into very high move speed across the screen, so light touches on the controller will send you to the borders of the play area. Certain enemies use very powerful attacks that cover that area, and it's really difficult stay out of their way. If you're thinking "well, it's a trade-off, some attacks become easier to dodge, others become more difficult", you're wrong. Even at the lowest speed, no attacks are particularly difficult to dodge, so making the ship fast beyond certain point plays against you. This kind of half-assed design permeates everything in the game. There's variability, but it's meaningless. The weapons are uninteresting and boring, the levels are uninteresting and boring. There's very little direction, design-wise. There's the core of a good game in there, but the execution is terrible. Edit, answer to devs: Fair enough. The game does feel more like one of those old arcade games than Star Fox (I haven't played Galaxy Force, but I played the heck out of After Burner back in the day, so I get the idea). I think my biggest gripe with the game is how "tenuous" the levels feel due to that old design style, where you pretty much have a background and stuff randomly comes at you from infinity. Star Fox 64 did a great job at making the levels feel solid. You're exploring as much as you're reacting to whatever the level throws at you. Makes it feel like a [i]place[/i] that you can [i]navigate,[/i] even if it's almost entirely on-rails. Despite my negative review, I appreciate the work and effort you put into your game, so I wanted to be a bit more constructive now that my original frustration has faded a bit. And, for what is worth, I thought the looks, the story, and the acting were pretty good. The boss battles do feel great for the most part, like the epic battles in Star Fox. Best of luck with your next game, I'll keep an eye out!

The game is fine. The first expression is better than the payoff. Great music. Nice Art in the outdoor levels. Pro: - Visual high speed spectacle graphics, espcially the sundown. - Special attack of the player looks really cool, nice gimmick - Great 80s rock ost. It has even japanese anime style opening, OMG! - Multiple endings, but... - Multiple weapons, but... - Nice anime style art, good voiced dialogue - Nice story, somewhat Alltynex inspired Neutral: - There are unlockable upgrades in the main menu, although you have to play the game for a while till you will unlock them. I do think this is conflict with the term of arcade game. A arcade game should not have this. And the gamemechanics are not complex enough to be a real roguelite game like Hades. - Its not like Star Fox 64. - Its more like Alltynex turned into 3D - Gameplay gets more exciting in new game plus. Con: - ...at least two of the multiple endings are boring to achieve. - ...the weapons don´t drop random, the upgrades are hardcoded into the chosen path. This is a lame concept - Only seven levels, no secret bosses. - Three paths, but path gamma and beta are just the same as alpha-path, but 1/3 shorter. Really missed potential - Bosses in overal have very simple and slow animations. The boss in stage 3 is veryyyy tedious. It cant get hit for over 30 seconds multiple times. - There is no level geometry like in Star Fox 64, its a endless skybox - The boss death animations are very unrealistic. Instead of crashing into a wall, crashing through the clouds oder submerging in lava they play simple explosive effects and slowly fade into distance. - Its easy to oversee if you are getting shot (much easier than Star Fox 64) - Most of the enemies are not really dangerous, aside from new game plus there it gets difficult. In short: I really like the visuals and the story. But the gameplay design, enemies, enemie-animations, level variaty not so much. Instead of 200 possible colour layouts the developer should have made the bosses more exciting. Music and voice acting is great tho, therefore I cant vote this down.

The art style is visually stunning. The gameplay and story are genuinely amazing; That being said I cannot recommend this game unless you pick it up on sale. I truly enjoyed my time playing the game, but I do not see myself returning to this title outside of the week I initially purchased it. I have beaten the game to 100% completion, and tried every mode on offer- but there is not THAT much replay value for me. I think the ROGUEFLIGHT mode would be much more interesting if the loadout equipped was changed every stage, adding more random difficulty. All being said, I actually find the story and characters pretty motivational, and feels unique enough to make me want more. I wish the game was about 2x the size it is currently, in regard to story progression. The endings are satisfying, and don't leave many questions unanswered- which is an extreme feat in its own right. I feel if the full run of NG+ or a potential 5th story ending featured 2-3 more locations with some unique enemies like the laser drones, the non-discounted asking price would be much more fair. I highly recommend the DEMO to any considering a purchase, as it is a great experience that is very true to the paid version of the game.

Fairly poor for a Star-Fox-like. I'm genuinely shocked the reviews for this are so high. Enemy bullets and missiles are hard to see, which is an absolute no-no for a shmup, and the only reason deaths aren't frequent is because you have a metric ton of health that recharges so long as you keep kill combos high. Your own shots are also hard to see, and aiming is unreliable because your shots don't line up with the crosshair most of the time, leading to you dancing around simply trying to hit enemies. Defeating enemies also doesn't really feel satisfying at all; you just roll around bullets while holding shoot down and they explode into explosion.jpg and get replaced by new ones and that's all of the levels. I guess you can also use the tailspin sword move if you feel like getting shot while dealing damage. The levels are also just skyboxes with enemies spawning in, a few levels try to throw obstacles at you but it pales in comparison to literally every other Star-Fox clone on the market. The presentation is the best part, and even then the game only looks kind of nice because of the overwhelming amount of filters it uses. The anime characters and the Arrow are the only models that look like they had any effort put into them. Also, I'm not sure why its called ROGUE Flight and tagged as a roguelite when it isn't even remotely anywhere near a roguelike or lite. Levels don't have random gear and upgrades in them. Nothing resets when you start a new "run". You get 4 different kinds of points which go to unlocking new upgrades that can be equipped any time outside of levels. I wasn't aware that having an upgrade system (that doesn't even improve the gameplay in any way by the way) made your game a roguelite??? I am shaking my head in real life. This really seems like someone made a space shooter mockup and was like "wow I could make money off of this" and dressed it up a bunch before releasing it on Steam without actually going back and making a proper fun video game.

Great game, but obviously very short. I did all 3 endings in 3h. And while there are other roguelike modes, I'm only interested in the mains story stuff. Man, I can only imagine what these guys would do if they had the budget of the new star fox game or somthing. This is a fantastic work of art. The problem is there's just not enough of it. The feeling, the voice acting and the atmosphere is there; the gameplay is also decent, but you're just left wanting more. I'm glad to be supporting a dev team that clearly made this a labor of love and an homage to older anime and games. But sadly, not many people seem to be willing to do that and now they probably won't be able to make another, more ambitious game. Sad.
